correctness.rationale: Polygon edge-strip and circular-sector moment computation proves the exact moment polynomial. Smooth or polygon approximation extends it to every convex body. Its barycentric conic has discriminant k(k-4)>0 by isoperimetric strictness, and its determinant of first and second derivatives equals 2ALπ det(H-G,S-G)/q³. For triangles, the exact barycentric determinant is A/(6Lπ) det(1,a_i,alpha_i); the sine rule and strictly concave sine establish noncollinearity iff all three angles are different. The divided-difference integral proves the stated positive Vandermonde lower bound. Isosceles center ordering follows from a strictly concave apex function and implies the exact nonvanishing axial derivative. Independent edge-sector numerical integration passed 875 cases; not substituted for universal proofs.

value.rationale: Curvature paths are a motivated geometric object in the foundational 2021 literature. The full conic/line dichotomy and exact triangle shape-rigidity boundary classify every natural three-vertex planar case; the quantitative angle-gap bound measures the stability of that boundary. These are structural geometric conditions on when reduction to a straight path is valid, not a numerical table, a name change, or an arbitrary finite slice. They do not claim a broader algorithmic theorem or an optimal constant.
